title: Rippling Alternatives Compared on Price and Fit
summary: Rippling alternatives vary in pricing and which modules they bundle. This comparison helps you find the option that covers only what your team needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Rippling more expensive than Gusto?


It depends on how many Rippling modules you buy, and Rippling's quote-only pricing makes that hard to check up front. Gusto publishes its plan tiers, so you can price a team before talking to anyone.


With Rippling you get a number only after a sales conversation, and each module you add changes it.


Ask both vendors for a quote covering only the modules you use, then compare those totals rather than the headline starting prices.


### Can I move from Rippling mid-year without redoing payroll?


Yes, but you'll have to load year-to-date wage and tax history into the new system, and that's where migrations tend to go wrong. If the new provider doesn't carry those balances, year-end forms such as W-2s won't match what you actually paid.


Before you commit, ask the new vendor how it imports prior-period payroll and who files for the earlier part of the year. Switching at the start of a quarter is cleaner, since there's less history to reconcile.


A free trial is a good place to run one import and check the balances against your last Rippling register.


### Which Rippling alternative is best for remote teams?


For a team in one country, pick the tool that files taxes in every state where you have employees, because that's where remote payroll usually breaks. Gusto is the most obvious fit for a US-only remote team.


If you hire across borders, a US payroll tool won't cover you, and you need an employer-of-record service, which becomes the legal employer in each country.


Test the exact setup you have: a hire in a state you haven't paid in before, and a contractor paid abroad.


### Does any alternative replace Rippling's IT management?


None of the payroll-first alternatives in this comparison does. Rippling's device and app management is a separate module that sits beside HR and payroll.


Most replacements stop at HR and payroll, so you'd cover IT with a dedicated device-management or identity tool.


This is why the module-matching advice matters: if you never used Rippling's IT features, you lose nothing by leaving them behind. If you did, price a separate tool into the switch.


### Is there a free Rippling alternative?


There's no free option that covers full payroll with tax filing for a growing team. Some HR tools have free tiers for records and time off, and those are worth a look if payroll isn't what you're replacing.


For payroll itself, use the vendor's free trial or demo account instead. Run a real pay cycle in it, check the tax calculations, and only then decide whether the price is worth paying.
